history.heading: Mesoamerican civilisations
paragraphs: Mexico was a cradle of civilisation in the Americas, where maize was domesticated about 9,000 years ago. The Olmecs, known for colossal stone heads, flourished from around 1200 BCE. Teotihuacan, with its Pyramids of the Sun and Moon, was one of the largest cities in the world in the first centuries CE. The Maya built cities such as Palenque and Chichén Itzá, and the Zapotecs built Monte Albán.
In the 14th century the Mexica (Aztecs) founded Tenochtitlan on an island in Lake Texcoco and built an empire that dominated central Mexico.

history.heading: Conquest and New Spain
paragraphs: Hernán Cortés arrived in 1519 and, allied with indigenous enemies of the Aztecs, conquered Tenochtitlan in 1521. Disease killed a large part of the indigenous population. Mexico City was built on the ruins of Tenochtitlan as the capital of the Viceroyalty of New Spain.
Silver mines made New Spain a major source of wealth for Spain, and a mestizo society blending indigenous and Spanish cultures developed. The Virgin of Guadalupe became a powerful national symbol.

history.heading: Independence and revolution
paragraphs: The priest Miguel Hidalgo launched the War of Independence in 1810, and Mexico became independent in 1821. The 19th century brought instability and war: Mexico lost about half its territory to the United States after the 1846–48 war, and France installed Emperor Maximilian before Benito Juárez restored the republic in 1867. Porfirio Díaz then ruled for over three decades.
The Mexican Revolution (1910–1920), with figures such as Emiliano Zapata and Pancho Villa, killed around a million people and produced the 1917 constitution with land reform and labour rights.

history.heading: Modern Mexico
paragraphs: The Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) governed for 71 years, until 2000. Mexico nationalised oil in 1938 and joined NAFTA with the US and Canada in 1994. The drug war launched in 2006 led to massive violence. In 2018 Andrés Manuel López Obrador won the presidency, and in 2024 Claudia Sheinbaum became Mexico's first female president.

culture.heading: A rich heritage
paragraphs: Spanish is the main language, and the government recognises 68 indigenous languages, including Nahuatl and Yucatec Maya. Mexico has one of the world's largest Catholic populations. It has more UNESCO World Heritage Sites than any other country in the Americas.
The Day of the Dead (Día de Muertos), honouring deceased loved ones with altars, marigolds and sugar skulls, is recognised by UNESCO, as is mariachi music.

culture.heading: Arts and food
paragraphs: Mexican muralists Diego Rivera, José Clemente Orozco and David Alfaro Siqueiros, and painter Frida Kahlo are world famous, as are writers Octavio Paz (Nobel laureate) and Juan Rulfo, and filmmakers such as Guillermo del Toro and Alfonso Cuarón.

Mexican cuisine, recognised by UNESCO, includes tacos, mole, tamales, pozole, chiles en nogada and guacamole, and drinks such as tequila and mezcal. Football is the most popular sport, and lucha libre wrestling is a cultural icon. Mexico co-hosted the 2026 World Cup with the United States and Canada, becoming the first country to host matches at three World Cups.

politics.heading: Federal republic
paragraphs: Mexico is a federal presidential republic of 32 states. The president is elected for a single six-year term (sexenio). Congress has a Chamber of Deputies and a Senate. The left-wing Morena party, founded by López Obrador, dominates politics. A controversial 2024 judicial reform introduced popular election of judges.
Organised crime and cartel violence, disappearances, corruption and migration are major issues. Relations with the United States centre on trade, migration, drug trafficking and tariffs.

economy.heading: A major manufacturing economy
paragraphs: Mexico has one of the largest economies in Latin America. It is a manufacturing powerhouse, closely integrated with the United States through the USMCA trade agreement, exporting cars, auto parts, electronics, machinery and medical devices. In 2023 it became the largest trading partner of the United States.

Oil, mining (Mexico is the world's largest silver producer), agriculture (avocados, tomatoes, berries) and tourism are also important. Remittances from Mexicans in the US are large. The currency is the peso.

economy.heading: Challenges
paragraphs: Mexico has high inequality, a large informal sector and regional gaps between the industrial north and the poorer south. Insecurity, low growth, dependence on the US market and the finances of state oil company Pemex are major challenges.
